chunk_findings.detail: `provider` returns `swarm.merged_per_hour` and `swarm.rework_rate` without applying `[metrics] min_samples`. Given `cfg.metrics.min_samples=10` and a context with one completed work item (`first_claim=0`, `completed_at=3600`, no failed outcomes and no bugs), `_merged` returns one span and `wall=3600`, so the provider emits `value=1.0` for `swarm.merged_per_hour` and `value=0.0` for `swarm.rework_rate`. The module contract says a figure under `min_samples` merged items is `None`, so `ddflow metrics` can show a baseline from too few items.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm_metrics.py:provider

chunk_findings.detail: `baseline` suppresses throughput, rework rate, and cost per item when `thin`, but leaves `critical_path` populated. Given `cfg.metrics.min_samples=10` and one merged item with `first_claim=0`, `completed_at=3600`, and `cycle_s=3600`, the result has `thin` true (`throughput.per_hour` and `rework.rate` are `None`) while `critical_path.length=1`, `critical_path.duration_s=3600.0`, `critical_path.slack_s=0.0`, and `critical_path.parallelism=1.0`. Those critical-path figures are derived from the under-sampled merged set and should be `None` under the module’s “figure under min_samples merged items is None” rule.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm_metrics.py:baseline

chunk_findings.detail: `provider()` returns `swarm.merged_per_hour` and `swarm.rework_rate` without consulting `cfg.metrics.min_samples`. Given `min_samples=10` and one merged item with no rework, it returns a non-None `swarm.merged_per_hour` and `swarm.rework_rate = 0.0`, whereas `baseline()` marks those figures as `None`/unavailable. This violates the module’s own contract that a figure under `[metrics] min_samples` merged items is `None`, never a zero, and `ddflow metrics` can display a zero rate from insufficient data.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm_metrics.py:provider

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts `targets == {"throughput": True, "cost": True, "rework": True}` for a before/after where `cost_per_item` rises from 2.0 to 2.4 (`cost_x == 1.2`, a 20% regression) and the rework rate worsens from 0.10 to 0.14. Because the stated intent is that the pilot must beat the baseline, a cost increase or rework increase must not be marked as meeting its target; this assertion would pass a `compare` implementation that treats real cost/rework regressions as successful.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_metrics.py:test_compare_against_targets
